Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a persistent, ill-defined opacity in the right upper lobe with possible spiculated margins and no significant volume loss (ruling out atelectasis) or cavitation (ruling out TB). In an adult with persistent focal opacity and worsening respiratory symptoms, this appearance is highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy, specifically adenocarcinoma, which can present as a peripheral mass or consolidative pattern with aerogenous spread.
